data.title: Easing
data.tagline: Control how motion speeds up and slows down
data.description: Easing changes the pace of a transition or animation over time. Ease-out often feels responsive for an element entering, while ease-in can suit an element leaving. Choose a small motion set and judge it in the real interaction, not from curve names alone.

use: Let an exiting element accelerate away
Give repeated interactions a consistent rhythm
Tune a transition without changing its path
avoid: Choose a curve only because its name sounds right
Use dramatic bounce for routine controls
Mix many easing curves in one flow
Make the beginning so slow that input feels delayed

lessonPractice.title: A modal should respond quickly and settle smoothly on entry, while exit should not delay the current task. How should its speed change?

options.label: Start entry fast and settle, accelerate exit, test against distance, and consolidate curves into tokens
options.feedback: Entry and exit serve different directions, so semantic testing plus reuse balances responsiveness and consistency.

options.label: Use linear for entry, exit, and continuous animation so every frame moves the same distance
options.feedback: Constant speed fits rotation or progress but often feels mechanical for interface movement and ignores direction.

options.label: Draw a different custom curve for every modal based only on how the current screen feels
options.feedback: Each may look acceptable alone, but arbitrary curves give peer interactions inconsistent and unpredictable rhythm.

data.agentPrompt: Choose task-appropriate easing for modal entry and exit: respond quickly and settle on entry, leave more decisively on exit. Test with actual travel distance, consolidate into a small motion-token set, and respect reduced motion.
